authorized: Implement real task orchestration without rewriting working components.
Add task and evidence contracts with provenance, validation and executed-only verification.
Add real shell execution, bounded retries, timeouts, cancellation, loop detection, circuit breaking and escalation.
Align documentation and claims with measured code.
Record honest limitations and external blockers.
prohibited: commit, merge, rebase, push, tag, publish or deploy
discarding or resetting unrelated user changes
claiming a pass from simulated, skipped or mocked execution

acceptanceCriteria: The orchestrator cannot report success unless a task was dispatched through a registered adapter.
Adapter output is schema-validated before it can affect task or mission state.
A task succeeds only when every required acceptance gate has a passing, non-simulated check.
Mission completion in executed mode requires evidence with provenance=executed and a non-empty executionId.
Timeouts, cancellation, retry exhaustion, loop detection and unavailable adapters produce explicit outcomes.
A real shell execution path is covered by a runtime test, not only mocks.
MCP, plugin and SDK remain contract-consistent; the full local ladder passes.
No commit or release occurs without separate authorization.
assumptions: The uncommitted Sprint 1/2 tree is the intended baseline.
A shell adapter executing the current Node binary is an acceptable real execution path for local verification.
The audit engine's security stage reflects the installed dependency tree, including pre-existing dev dependencies.
unknowns: Whether the host approval UI exists for escalated governance decisions.
Whether a production Postgres server is available for live integration testing.
Whether the pre-existing dev-dependency advisories can be upgraded without a network install.
definitionOfFunctional: A mission plan is created, governed, dispatched to a registered execution adapter, validated against acceptance criteria, recorded as executed evidence, and only then completed; every failure path terminates or escalates explicitly and is reproducible from tests.
